topics.title: Surface area and volume of solids

learn.hook: Ice-cream cones, cricket balls and gas cylinders — every solid has a 'skin' (surface area) and a 'filling' (volume)!
points: Cuboid: TSA = 2(lb + bh + hl), volume = lbh. Cube: TSA = 6a², volume = a³.
Cylinder: curved surface area (CSA) = 2πrh, TSA = 2πr(r + h), volume = πr²h.
Cone: slant height l = √(r² + h²), CSA = πrl, TSA = πr(l + r), volume = ⅓πr²h.
Sphere: surface area = 4πr², volume = (4/3)πr³. Hemisphere: CSA = 2πr², TSA = 3πr², volume = (2/3)πr³.
Surface area is in square units (cm²); volume is in cubic units (cm³).

example.q: Find the volume of a cone with radius 7 cm and height 12 cm. (π = 22/7)

learn.reallife: A painter needs surface area to buy paint for a water tank, and a milkman needs volume to know how much milk his can holds.

quiz.q: A cone has radius 6 cm and height 8 cm. What is its slant height?
quiz.mistake: Adds r and h (14 cm) instead of using Pythagoras

quiz.q: What is the volume of a sphere of radius 3 cm?
quiz.mistake: Uses r² instead of r³, or forgets the 4/3

quiz.q: What is the curved surface area of a cylinder with radius 7 cm and height 10 cm? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Includes the two circular ends (TSA = 748 cm²)

quiz.q: What is the total surface area of a solid hemisphere of radius 7 cm? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: TSA = curved part 2πr² + flat circle πr² = 3πr² = 3 × 154 = 462 cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses only the curved part 2πr² = 308 cm²

quiz.q: What is the volume of a cone with radius 3 cm and height 7 cm? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Forgets the ⅓ and gives the cylinder's volume

quiz.q: What is the total surface area of a cube with edge 5 cm?
quiz.explain: A cube has 6 square faces: 6 × 5² = 150 cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses only 4 faces (100 cm²) or gives the volume (125)

quiz.q: A cylinder and a cone have the same base radius and the same height. What is the ratio of their volumes (cylinder : cone)?
quiz.explain: Cylinder = πr²h and cone = ⅓πr²h, so the cylinder holds 3 times as much.
quiz.mistake: Writes the ratio the wrong way round

quiz.q: A round laddoo is a sphere of radius 2 cm. What is its surface area?
quiz.explain: 4πr² = 4 × π × 4 = 16π cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses the volume formula and gets 32π/3

teach.ask: Gappu holds an ice-cream cone: 'What's the difference between its surface area and its volume?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Surface area covers the outside in square units; volume fills the inside in cubic units!
teach.nudge: Which one is about covering and which is about filling — and what units does each use?

learn.hook: A toy top is a cone stuck on a hemisphere — to paint it, count only the surfaces you can actually touch!
points: A combined solid is made by joining two or more basic solids.
Its surface area = sum of the surfaces that remain visible on the outside.
Faces that are glued together are hidden, so they are NOT counted.
So the surface area of a combination is usually LESS than the sum of the separate total surface areas.
Draw a sketch and list each exposed part before adding.

example.q: A tent is a cylinder of radius 7 m and height 3 m with a cone of slant height 10 m on top. How much canvas is needed (no floor)? (π = 22/7)
steps: Floor and joined circles are not canvas

learn.reallife: Tent makers at a mela, toy makers and painters of temple domes all work out only the visible surface.

games.title: Visible or hidden?
items: When a cone sits on a hemisphere, the cone's circular base is not part of the outer surface.
It is glued to the hemisphere's flat face and hidden.
The surface area of a combined solid is the sum of the TSAs of its parts.
The joined faces are hidden, so they must be left out.
The surface of a capsule = two hemispheres + the curved surface of a cylinder.
The flat ends are hidden where the parts join.
To paint the outside of a hemispherical dome, you paint 2πr².
Only the curved part is outside; the flat base sits on the building.
Two identical cubes joined face to face have total surface area 12a².
Two faces get hidden, leaving 10a².
If a hemisphere is scooped out of the top of a cylinder, the inside curved surface 2πr² is added.
The hollow bowl surface is new, while the top circle is removed.

items.text: Cone on a hemisphere: surface = πrl + ___
Two cubes of edge 4 cm joined face to face: surface area = ___ cm²
Tent without floor = curved surface of cylinder + ___

quiz.q: Two cubes of edge 5 cm are joined end to end. What is the surface area of the cuboid formed?
quiz.explain: Each cube has 6 faces of 25 cm²; joining hides 2 faces. 10 × 25 = 250 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds the two TSAs (300 cm²) without removing the hidden faces

quiz.q: A capsule is a cylinder of length 10 cm and radius 3.5 cm with a hemisphere on each end. What is its surface area? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cylinder curved part = 2 × 22/7 × 3.5 × 10 = 220 cm². Two hemispheres = 4πr² = 4 × 22/7 × 12.25 = 154 cm². Total = 374 cm².
quiz.mistake: Counts the hemispheres twice over or adds the hidden ends

quiz.q: A toy is a cone of radius 3 cm and height 4 cm on a hemisphere of radius 3 cm. What is its total surface area?
quiz.explain: Slant height = 5 cm, so cone CSA = π × 3 × 5 = 15π. Hemisphere CSA = 2π × 9 = 18π. Total = 33π cm².
quiz.mistake: Uses the hemisphere's TSA (3πr²) and gets 42π

quiz.q: A tent is a cylinder of radius 7 m and height 5 m topped by a cone of slant height 9 m. How much canvas is needed (no floor)? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cylinder walls = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 5 = 220 m². Cone = 22/7 × 7 × 9 = 198 m². Total = 418 m².
quiz.mistake: Adds the floor (154 m²) as well

quiz.q: A hemisphere is fixed on top of a cylinder of the same radius. Which surfaces are hidden?
options: The curved surface of the cylinder
The flat face of the hemisphere and the top of the cylinder
quiz.explain: The flat circle of the hemisphere sits exactly on the top circle of the cylinder, so both are hidden.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the bottom base is hidden because it sits on the table

quiz.q: A cube of edge 14 cm has a hemisphere of diameter 14 cm fixed on top. What is the surface area of the solid? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cube = 6 × 196 = 1176 cm². The hemisphere adds 2πr² but covers πr² of the top, a net gain of πr² = 154 cm². Total = 1330 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds 2πr² but forgets that it covers part of the cube's top

quiz.q: A solid cylinder of radius 7 cm and height 10 cm has a hemisphere of the same radius scooped out from its top. What is the total surface area? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Curved side 440 + bottom circle 154 + inside bowl 2πr² = 308. The top circle is gone. Total = 902 cm².
quiz.mistake: Keeps the top circle that was scooped away

quiz.q: A Diwali lamp-shade model is a cone (radius 7 cm, slant height 25 cm) on a hollow cylinder (radius 7 cm, height 6 cm), open at the bottom. What is its outer surface area? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cone = 22/7 × 7 × 25 = 550 cm². Cylinder side = 2 × 22/7 × 7 × 6 = 264 cm². Total = 814 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds the open bottom circle (154 cm²)

teach.ask: Gappu glued a cone onto a hemisphere: 'Do I just add both total surface areas to paint it?'
teach.praise: Tweet tweet! Add only the visible surfaces — the glued parts don't need paint!
teach.nudge: What happens to the faces that are stuck together?

topics.title: Everyday combined solids and painting costs

learn.hook: A capsule, a tent, a test tube and a kulfi cone — look closely and each is just two simple solids stuck together!
points: Many objects are two basic solids joined: a capsule (cylinder + two hemispheres), a tent (cylinder + cone), a test tube (cylinder + hemisphere), an ice-cream cone (cone + hemisphere).
Cost of painting, polishing or canvas = (area to be covered) × (rate per unit area).
The largest hemisphere that fits on a face of a cube of edge a has diameter a (radius a/2).
When a hemisphere sits on a cube face, the cube loses a circle of area πr² but the hemisphere adds 2πr². So the total surface area = 6a² + πr².
For a cone, find the slant height first: l = √(h² + r²).

example.q: A cube of edge 7 cm has the largest possible hemisphere fixed on top. Find the surface area of the solid. (π = 22/7)
steps: Largest hemisphere: diameter = 7 cm, so r = 3.5 cm
Hidden circle: −πr²; hemisphere curved surface: +2πr²; net +πr²

learn.reallife: Tent makers price canvas by the square metre, and painters charge by area — so combined-solid surface areas turn straight into rupees.

Cost of 143 m² at ₹200 per m² (₹)

quiz.q: Which object is a cylinder with a hemisphere at each end?
quiz.explain: A capsule (medicine tablet) is a cylinder with two hemispherical ends.
quiz.mistake: Mixes up which object has which parts

quiz.q: An ice-cream cone filled and topped with a scoop is made of which solids?
quiz.explain: The wafer is a cone and the rounded scoop on top is a hemisphere.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the scoop is a cylinder

quiz.q: A test tube is made of which two solids?
quiz.explain: A test tube is a cylinder closed at the bottom by a hemisphere.
quiz.mistake: Thinks the rounded end is a cone

quiz.q: The largest possible hemisphere is fixed on top of a cube of edge 7 cm. What is the surface area of the solid? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: r = 3.5 cm. Total = 6a² − πr² + 2πr² = 294 + 38.5 = 332.5 cm².
quiz.mistake: Adds the hemisphere's curved surface but forgets to remove the hidden circle (gets 371)

quiz.q: What is the greatest diameter of a hemisphere that can sit on a face of a cube of edge 10 cm?
quiz.explain: The circular base must fit inside the square face, so its diameter can be at most the edge, 10 cm.
quiz.mistake: Gives the radius instead of the diameter

quiz.q: A hemispherical dome of radius 7 m is painted on the outside at ₹10 per m². What is the cost? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Curved surface = 2πr² = 2 × (22/7) × 49 = 308 m². Cost = 308 × 10 = ₹3080.
quiz.mistake: Uses the TSA 3πr² (includes the floor) or forgets the factor 2

quiz.q: A tent is a cylinder (radius 3.5 m, height 4 m) with a cone (slant height 5 m) on top. Canvas costs ₹200 per m². What is the cost of canvas (no floor)? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Includes the floor, or uses only one part

quiz.q: A toy is a cone (radius 3.5 cm, height 12 cm) on a hemisphere of the same radius. What is the area to be painted? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Uses the height 12 instead of the slant height

teach.ask: Gappu wants to paint a toy that is a cone on a hemisphere. How should he work out the area and the cost?
teach.praise: Chirp! Add the visible curved surfaces (using the slant height), then multiply by the rate!
teach.nudge: Which surfaces of the toy actually get paint?

learn.hook: How much ice-cream fits in a cone with a scoop on top? Just add the volumes!
points: Volume of a combined solid = sum of the volumes of its parts (they don't overlap).
If a part is cut out or scooped away, subtract its volume.
Unlike surface area, no volume is 'hidden' when solids are joined.
1 litre = 1000 cm³.
Keep the answer in terms of π when the question allows — it avoids rounding errors.

example.q: An ice-cream cone has radius 3 cm and height 6 cm, with a hemisphere of ice-cream of radius 3 cm on top. Find the total volume.

learn.reallife: Dairy workers and gas companies find the volume of capsule-shaped tankers this way to know how much they can carry.

quiz.q: An ice-cream cone has radius 3 cm and height 4 cm, filled and topped with a hemisphere of radius 3 cm. What is the total volume of ice-cream?
quiz.explain: Cone = ⅓π × 9 × 4 = 12π. Hemisphere = (2/3)π × 27 = 18π. Total = 30π cm³.
quiz.mistake: Uses a full sphere (36π) instead of a hemisphere

quiz.q: A solid is a cylinder (radius 7 cm, height 6 cm) with a cone of the same radius and height 6 cm on top. What is its volume? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Cylinder = 22/7 × 49 × 6 = 924 cm³. Cone = ⅓ × 924 = 308 cm³. Total = 1232 cm³.
quiz.mistake: Treats the cone as having the same volume as the cylinder

quiz.q: A capsule is a cylinder of radius 3 cm and length 10 cm with a hemisphere at each end. What is its volume?
quiz.explain: Cylinder = π × 9 × 10 = 90π. Two hemispheres make a sphere = (4/3)π × 27 = 36π. Total = 126π cm³.
quiz.mistake: Adds only one hemisphere (108π)

quiz.q: A cone of the same base and height is carved out of a solid cylinder of radius 3 cm and height 5 cm. What volume is left?
quiz.explain: Cylinder = π × 9 × 5 = 45π. Cone = ⅓ × 45π = 15π. Remaining = 30π cm³ (two-thirds of the cylinder).
quiz.mistake: Gives the cone's volume instead of what is left

quiz.q: A wooden toy is a hemisphere of radius 7 cm topped with a cone of the same radius and height 7 cm. What is its volume? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Gives the volume of only one part

quiz.q: Two cubes, each of volume 27 cm³, are joined end to end. What is the volume of the cuboid formed?
quiz.explain: No volume is lost when solids are joined, so 27 + 27 = 54 cm³.
quiz.mistake: Thinks joining hides some volume, as it does for surface area

quiz.q: Why can we add the volumes of the parts but not their total surface areas?
options: Joined faces are hidden from the surface, but all the space inside still counts
Volume is always bigger than surface area
Surface area is measured in cm³
We can add both in every case
quiz.explain: When solids are joined, the touching faces disappear from the outside, but none of the space inside is lost.
quiz.mistake: Treats surface area and volume the same way

quiz.q: Harpreet's water bottle is a cylinder of radius 3.5 cm and height 20 cm. How much water does it hold? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Volume = 22/7 × 12.25 × 20 = 770 cm³. Since 1 L = 1000 cm³, that is 0.77 L.
quiz.mistake: Divides by 100 instead of 1000 when converting to litres

teach.ask: Gappu stuck a scoop of ice-cream on a cone: 'How much ice-cream is there altogether?'
teach.praise: Chirp! Find the volume of each part and add them. That's a lot of ice-cream!
teach.nudge: What do I find for each part, and how do I combine them?

topics.title: Pen stands, overflowing water and tricky glasses

learn.hook: Drop a marble into a glass filled to the brim — exactly the marble's volume spills out. Archimedes would be proud!
points: When a part is removed (holes in a pen stand, a hemisphere carved out), subtract its volume: remaining = whole − removed.
A solid fully dropped into a full vessel pushes out water equal to its own volume. In a partly full vessel, the water level rises by (volume of solid) ÷ (base area).
Number of small solids = total volume needed ÷ volume of one.
A glass with a raised hemispherical bottom LOOKS like a full cylinder, but its real capacity = cylinder volume − hemisphere volume.

example.q: A wooden pen stand is a cuboid 12 cm × 8 cm × 5 cm with 3 conical holes, each of radius 1 cm and depth 2.1 cm. Find the volume of wood. (π = 22/7)

learn.reallife: Kitchens and labs use 'overflow' to measure the volume of odd-shaped things like a potato or a stone — just catch the water that spills out!

games.title: Water and a dropped solid
items: Find the volume of the solid dropped in
This equals the volume of water pushed up or out
Find the base area of the vessel
Rise in level = volume of solid ÷ base area
Check the units (cm³ ÷ cm² = cm)

games.title: True or false?
items: A fully dropped solid pushes out water equal to its own volume.
This is the displacement idea.
Holes in a pen stand increase the volume of wood.
Wood is removed, so you subtract.
A raised bottom makes a glass hold less than it seems.
Subtract the hemisphere from the cylinder.
Rise in water level = volume of solid × base area.
Divide by the base area.
Number of balls = total volume ÷ volume of one ball.
That counts how many fit the volume.

quiz.q: A wooden pen stand is a cuboid 12 cm × 8 cm × 5 cm with 3 conical holes, each of radius 1 cm and depth 2.1 cm. What volume of wood is in it? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Adds the holes instead of subtracting them

quiz.q: What is the volume of ONE conical hole in that pen stand (radius 1 cm, depth 2.1 cm)? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Forgets the 1/3 in the cone formula

quiz.q: A glass is filled to the brim with water. A solid metal sphere of radius 2.1 cm is dropped in and sinks. How much water spills out? (π = 22/7)
quiz.explain: Spilled water = volume of sphere = (4/3)(22/7)(2.1)³ = (4/3)(22/7)(9.261) = 38.808 cm³.
quiz.mistake: Uses the surface area 4πr² instead of the volume

quiz.q: A conical vessel (radius 6 cm, height 8 cm) is full of water. Metal balls of radius 1 cm are dropped in until one-fourth of the water has flowed out. How many balls are dropped?
quiz.explain: Cone = (1/3)π(36)(8) = 96π. One-fourth = 24π. One ball = (4/3)π. Number = 24π ÷ (4/3)π = 18.
quiz.mistake: Uses the whole volume of water instead of one-fourth

quiz.q: A glass has inner radius 3 cm and height 10 cm, but its bottom has a raised hemisphere of radius 3 cm. What is its APPARENT capacity (as a plain cylinder)? (π = 3.14)
quiz.explain: Apparent capacity = πr²h = 3.14 × 9 × 10 = 282.6 cm³.
quiz.mistake: Subtracts the hemisphere already (that is the actual capacity)

quiz.q: What is the ACTUAL capacity of that glass (radius 3 cm, height 10 cm, raised hemisphere of radius 3 cm)? (π = 3.14)
quiz.mistake: Adds the hemisphere instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: A solid is dropped into a vessel filled to the brim and is fully covered by water. How much water flows out?
options: Equal to the surface area of the solid
Equal to the volume of the vessel
No water flows out at all
Equal to the volume of the solid
quiz.explain: The solid takes up space equal to its own volume, so that much water is pushed out.
quiz.mistake: Confuses surface area with volume

quiz.q: A cylindrical jar of radius 7 cm has some water in it. A solid sphere of radius 3.5 cm is dropped in and is fully covered. By how much does the water level rise?
quiz.explain: Rise = sphere volume ÷ base area = (4/3)π(3.5)³ ÷ π(7)² = (4/3)(42.875)/49 = 7/6 cm.
quiz.mistake: Divides by the jar's volume instead of its base area

teach.ask: Gappu drops a marble into a full glass of water. Explain how much water spills and how to find the real capacity of a glass with a raised bottom.
teach.praise: Tweet! The spill equals the marble's volume — and the raised bottom must be subtracted from the cylinder!
teach.nudge: What about the raised bump at the bottom of the glass — do we add it or take it away?

topics.title: Sheds, iron poles and chapter recap

learn.hook: How much air is inside a shed with a curved roof? How heavy is an iron pole made of two cylinders? Let's find out!
points: A shed with a curved roof is often a cuboid with a half-cylinder on top. Volume = cuboid + ½ × πr²l (l = length of the shed).
Air inside = volume of the shed − volume taken up by machines, people and so on.
A pole made of two cylinders: add the two volumes, π r₁²h₁ + π r₂²h₂. Mass = volume × density.
Recap: surface area of a combination = sum of the exposed surfaces only; volume of a combination = sum of the volumes of the parts (subtract any part removed).

example.q: A shed is a cuboid 10 m long, 7 m wide and 4 m high, with a half-cylinder roof of diameter 7 m running along its length. Find its volume. (π = 22/7)

learn.reallife: Warehouse planners compute the air volume of a shed to size fans and air-conditioners; engineers compute pole masses to choose cranes.

games.title: Recap check
items: Volume of a combined solid = sum of the volumes of its parts.
No volume is hidden when solids are joined.
Surface area of a combined solid = sum of the TSAs of its parts.
Joined faces are hidden and are not counted.
If a part is hollowed out, its volume is subtracted.
Remaining = whole − removed.
Mass = volume × density.
For example, 1000 cm³ of iron at 8 g/cm³ is 8000 g.
A half-cylinder roof has volume πr²l.
It is half of that: ½πr²l.

quiz.q: A shed is a cuboid 10 m × 7 m × 4 m with a half-cylinder roof of diameter 7 m along its 10 m length. What is its volume? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Uses a full cylinder for the roof, or the diameter as the radius

quiz.q: In that shed (volume 472.5 m³), machines take up 50 m³ and 10 workers take up 0.08 m³ each. How much air is inside?
quiz.mistake: Forgets to multiply 0.08 by the number of workers

quiz.q: An iron pole is a cylinder of radius 10 cm and height 100 cm with a cylinder of radius 5 cm and height 40 cm on top. What is its volume? (π = 3.14)
quiz.mistake: Forgets the smaller cylinder or squares the height instead of the radius

quiz.q: Iron has a density of 8 g per cm³. What is the mass of that pole (volume 34540 cm³) in kg?
quiz.mistake: Divides by the density instead of multiplying

quiz.q: Recap: how do you find the total surface area of a solid made by joining two basic solids?
options: Add the TSAs of both parts
Use only the bigger solid's TSA
Add only the surfaces that remain exposed
quiz.explain: The faces that are glued together are hidden, so only the exposed surfaces are added.
quiz.mistake: Adds the full TSAs and counts hidden faces

quiz.q: Recap: a solid is a cylinder (radius 7 cm, height 10 cm) with a hemisphere of radius 7 cm on top. What is its volume? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Uses a full sphere instead of a hemisphere (gets 2977.33)

quiz.q: Recap: a hemisphere of radius 3.5 cm is hollowed out of a cube of edge 7 cm. What volume remains? (π = 22/7)
quiz.mistake: Adds the hemisphere instead of subtracting it

quiz.q: Recap: which formula gives the volume of a cone?
quiz.explain: A cone holds one-third of a cylinder with the same base and height: ⅓πr²h.
quiz.mistake: Confuses the volume with the curved surface area πrl

teach.ask: Gappu wants to know how much air is inside a shed with a curved roof. Explain the steps.
teach.praise: Chirp! Add the cuboid and the half-cylinder, then take away what the machines and people fill!
teach.nudge: What shape is the curved roof, and how much of a cylinder is it?
